How water works on your site

Three kinds of water move across your plot: the fresh water you use, the rain that falls, and the used water that leaves the house. This plan gives each one its own route. Drinking water stays clean, rain is stored or returned to the ground, and storm water is held on your land.

    Edit the layout

    Drag the sump, septic tank, soak pit or pond on the plan, or type a new position and size. Capacities, pipe levels, drawings, the 3D model, the sheets and the cost update with every change, and each item is checked against the clearances it needs.

    Arrow keys nudge the selected item by 6 inches; hold Shift for 5 ft.

    The faint background is your designer's drawing, so it still shows the original positions. Pipes to a moved item are redrawn as straight runs; the final route is set on site.

      Cost estimate

      A first budget, measured from this layout. The rates are indicative Hyderabad-area rates for finished work with labour. Change any rate below and the totals follow; swap in contractor quotes when you have them.

      ItemQtyUnitRate ₹Amount
      Change the rates

      Not included: the pool shell and finishes, electrical supply and cabling, rock excavation or dewatering, design fees and GST. Material prices were checked against Hyderabad market prices (May 2026); the sump works out near the top of the usual ₹8–20 per litre range for built RCC sumps, and the recharge items sit within published rainwater-harvesting costs. Built-work rates are estimates, not quotes.

      Pipe layout schedule

      Inverts for the gravity lines were set from each outlet working upstream, so every run falls continuously. Cover is to the proposed finished ground.
